title: Security: instantsearch.js 4.86.0 pins vulnerable preact@10.28.0 (CVE-2026-22028)
body:
### 🐛 Current behavior

Hi team 👋

`instantsearch.js@4.86.0` depends on `preact@10.28.0`, which is affected by
CVE-2026-22028 (HIGH).

The issue is fixed in `preact@10.28.2`, but the dependency is currently pinned,
causing `npm audit` / `pnpm audit` to fail.

Dependency chain:
react-instantsearch@7.22.0
└─ instantsearch.js@4.86.0
  └─ preact@10.28.0

Suggested fix:
- bump preact to `^10.28.2`

Workaround:
- using package manager overrides

Thanks!

### 🔍 Steps to reproduce

1. Create a new project
2. Install react-instantsearch 7.22.0

   npm install react-instantsearch@7.22.0

3. Run a security audit

   npm audit
   # or pnpm audit / yarn audit

4. Observe the following vulnerability report:

   - Package: preact
   - Installed version: 10.28.0
   - CVE: CVE-2026-22028 (HIGH)
   - Dependency path:
     react-instantsearch@7.22.0
     └─ instantsearch.js@4.86.0
        └─ preact@10.28.0


### Live reproduction

https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/github/algolia/instantsearch/tree/templates/instantsearch.js

### 💭 Expected behavior

`instantsearch.js` should not pin a vulnerable version of `preact`.

The dependency should be updated to a patched version (`>= 10.28.2`) so that
installing `react-instantsearch` / `instantsearch.js` does not trigger a
HIGH severity security advisory during `npm audit`, `pnpm audit`, or
`yarn audit`.


### Package version

instantsearch.js 4.86.0, react-instantsearch 7.22.0

### Operating system

_No response_

### Browser

_No response_

comments.body:
The preact dependency isn't pinned, it's `^10.10.0`: https://github.com/algolia/instantsearch/blob/aca8934163c047ca56db0dad679737f331efac29/packages/instantsearch.js/package.json#L39

The affected versions are 10.26.5 - 10.28.1, so that means we are actually not explicitly dependent on 10.28.0 as you mention. 

The vulnerability would happen if a non-serialised object gets rendered, which would be possible with htm templates if you explicitly choose so.

It still seems interesting to bump the minimum to 10.28.2

Additionally, if you are using InstantSearch via React InstantSearch, this vulnerability can't be exposed to you, as no preact rendering happens in React InstantSearch.

Hi @Haroenv 

We're seeing the same high-severity vulnerability reported by `yarn audit --groups dependencies`. Because this package is deployed to production, our security team has opened an alert. Will there be a react-instantsearch release that updates `preact to ^10.28.2`? If not, could you suggest any short-term mitigations we can apply until a release is available?

For reference, we're using `react-instantsearch@7.22.1`.


Thank you,
Arindam

> any short-term mitigations we can apply until a release is available

You can change your lockfile or install a correct preact version yourself, you don't need to wait for a release

I just did a test installing the latest React InstantSearch and I get preact 10.28.2, so this is an issue with your own lockfile you can solve by updating (`yarn upgrade preact` for example)
